guidance: A field reader, not a validator: the bytes are trusted, and a message that parses is not necessarily one a host should accept. The checksum covers the ICMP message alone, so a paste cut short of the whole message cannot verify, and a network card with checksum offload can leave a placeholder in an outbound capture. ICMPv6 is refused because its checksum covers a pseudo-header and its type registry is a different one. This page makes no capture, sends no probe and reads no traffic.
method: Fields are read at the offsets RFC 792 gives them: a type octet, a code octet, a 16-bit checksum, then four bytes whose meaning depends on the type. The checksum is the 16-bit one's complement of the one's complement sum of the message starting at the type, with the checksum field zeroed and a final odd octet padded with a zero, so a message carrying the right value sums to 0xFFFF; the value reported as expected is the complement of the same sum. The rest-of-header field is decoded where a standard defines it: echo and information messages carry an identifier and sequence number, a fragmentation-needed message carries the next-hop MTU in the low 16 bits (RFC 1191, where zero means a router that did not report one), redirect carries a gateway address, parameter problem carries a byte pointer, timestamp carries three millisecond counters, address mask carries a mask, and router advertisement carries a count, an entry size in 32-bit words, a lifetime and a list of addresses with signed preference levels (RFC 1256). Destination unreachable, source quench, redirect, time exceeded and parameter problem quote the original datagram's IPv4 header and the first 64 bits of its data (RFC 792), so that inner header is parsed and its quoted length is compared with the original total length; source and destination ports are read when the inner protocol is TCP or UDP and at least four data bytes were quoted. Type and code names come from the IANA ICMP parameters registry, and a name the registry marks Deprecated is printed with that word. A complete IPv4 packet whose protocol field is 1 is unwrapped before decoding, a packet carrying another protocol is refused rather than read as ICMP, and an IPv6 packet is refused because ICMPv6 has its own types and a pseudo-header checksum. A non-zero unused field is called out, codes outside a type's registry are named Unassigned, and types with no code registry are named Not specified. Everything is calculated in the browser; nothing is sent, stored or uploaded.
